title: Quantum Matter
subtitle: Small rules. Rich structures.
description: Explore states, bonding, and the models that connect microscopic rules to the materials around us.
sequence: Connect a model to a property
Check what a measurement can tell you
prompt: For a fixed two-outcome quantum measurement, must the probabilities of its possible outcomes add up to one?
answer: Yes. The probabilities of all possible outcomes of the specified measurement must sum to one. Changing the state can change those probabilities; the measurement setup defines the outcomes being considered.

title: Fluid Dynamics
subtitle: See the motion inside the flow.
description: Follow streamlines, reason about conservation, and build intuition for how geometry changes a flow.
sequence: Use conservation to make a prediction
prompt: A steady, incompressible flow passes through a pipe with no leaks. If its cross-sectional area halves, what happens to the mean flow speed?
answer: It doubles. Under these assumptions the volume flow rate is constant, so area multiplied by mean speed stays the same. The conclusion depends on the stated steady-flow, incompressibility, and no-leak assumptions.

title: Plasma Dynamics
subtitle: Charged motion. Collective questions.
description: Begin with a moving charge, then explore how fields, particle motion, and collective behavior shape plasma models.
sequence: Connect the particle picture to a plasma model
prompt: A charged particle moves exactly parallel to a uniform magnetic field. With no electric field present, is the magnetic force zero?
answer: Yes. The magnetic force is proportional to the cross product of velocity and magnetic field. Parallel vectors give a zero cross product. This single-particle example is a starting point, not a complete plasma model.

title: Electrodynamics
subtitle: Think in fields, not just objects.
description: Connect charge, current, electric and magnetic fields, and the waves that carry their changes through space.
prompt: For a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum, how are the electric field, magnetic field, and propagation direction arranged?
answer: The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another, and both are perpendicular to the direction of propagation. This description applies to the plane-wave setup specified in the question.

title: Space–time
subtitle: A different frame for an event.
description: Work with events, reference frames, and light cones to ask what can influence what—and how a diagram encodes it.
prompt: In a spacetime diagram, what does the light cone around an event help you distinguish?
answer: It distinguishes events that can be causally connected to the chosen event from events outside that causal reach. A light cone describes possible influence; it is not a picture of an object moving faster than light.

title: Intuition
subtitle: Mind, connected.
description: Explore intuition through logic, mathematics, and a conceptual model of Mind. Ego traces a place-and-time decision path shaped by knowledge, strategy, observation, and end-to-end orchestration.
sequence: Test the result and decide the next action
prompt: If P implies Q, and Q is true, must P also be true?
answer: No. The converse needs its own justification. For example, every multiple of 4 is even, but 6 is even without being a multiple of 4. One counterexample is enough to disprove a claim that is supposed to hold in every case.
source_name: MIT OpenCourseWare · Mathematics for Computer Science

title: Singularity
subtitle: Bring knowledge into one view.
description: Connect ideas across physics, mathematics, and computation. Build a coherent view of what you know, how the pieces relate, and which questions open the next direction.
sequence: Choose ideas from two learning paths
Build a synthesis and identify a new question
prompt: Choose two ideas from earlier paths. What connects them, where do they differ, and what new question follows?
answer: Build a small concept map. Label a connection, name a difference, and state which assumptions make the connection useful. Treat the map as a synthesis to refine, and check factual claims against the sources for each path.
